variants.name: Кальтропы 01 · Тёмная сталь
variants.prompt:
Edit the provided tile to add a NATURAL RANDOM SCATTER of LOOSE NINJA CALTROPS. The tile in the image is the exact approved in-game reference: keep the same blue-grey cracked top, thick masonry sides, framing, size, camera, transparent background and 4:3 diamond. No other tile or base. Whole tile and all objects must fit in frame.

CRITICAL ART DIRECTION: this must unmistakably look like someone tossed a handful of small independent metal objects onto the floor, NOT a constructed spiked floor or a patterned trap. Visibly chaotic non-grid placement. Different rotation for EVERY object: their feet and arms point at strongly different angles, some are foreshortened, some point toward the viewer, some sideways, some seen end-on. Natural tiny pairs and loose asymmetric clusters alternate with irregular gaps. No rows, columns, lattice, evenly spaced dots, identical orientations, aligned axes, symmetric composition or centre pile. Each caltrop is a recognizable small hand-forged FOUR-ARM jack/tetrahedral metal tool with long thin tapered arms spreading out from a central knot: three splayed contact feet REST ON THE STONE and a fourth point is upward or diagonally up. They are freestanding objects with a little contact shadow. They have horizontal spreading arms, NOT pyramidal triangles standing on a base and NOT upright spikes emerging from stone. No holes, no mounting plate, no ground stakes. Scatter covers the WHOLE upper diamond, near back/front and both side edges too; not just a central zone. Keep masonry side faces uncovered. Crisp coherent game art matching the reference, without additional coarse pixel grid, no text, no extra props, no characters.

Variant 01: approximately 20 dark iron jack-shaped ninja caltrops with silver sharpened tips. An asymmetrical thrown scatter with a few loose pairs near opposite edges and several isolated pieces between. Obvious differences in angle and foreshortening. Compact but clearly loose four-armed objects, not a field of upright triangles.
